D10 was taken by recommendation (goal cap = min(remaining, org per-run ceiling), never above the org's) and built dark; the owner must confirm before switch-on.

A Do run carries no per-run token or USD cap to execution-core (register D2-705), so goal_turn_cap is only logged at claim. One goal turn can overshoot the remaining budget by a whole run, and the goal stops only at its next claim.

The settle runs in the follower stream. A run that outlives the follow deadline, or a replica that dies, is settled 'unknown' or 'lease_expired' with no usage, and its tokens are lost unless a later settle names the run; moving the settle into the dispatch task, as AgentUsageLedger did, would close this.

A goal turn that ends awaiting_approval or parked is settled then. The tokens its later /continue segment spends are never debited, because the continuation passes goal_turn None and the settle is idempotent on the run.
Settle and drop-settle use the turn's user session bearer (~300 s). A long run's settle can be refused with an expired credential, leaving the turn to lease expiry and losing its usage.

The claim lease (30 min, D11) can be shorter than a pinned run's follow deadline. An expiring lease then lets a second turn be claimed while the first still runs; the late settle adds the first turn's usage once.

SettleGoalTurn trusts the caller's usage figures and accepts any owner bearer. Only the gateway calls it today, but restricting it to a gateway service principal would stop a direct gRPC caller from under-reporting spend.
